findings.title: Missing re-check of cache after acquiring write lock causes duplicate expensive loads
findings.body: GetWebAssets uses a read-then-write lock pattern, but after releasing the read lock and acquiring the write lock (line 48), it never re-checks whether another goroutine populated entryPointAssetsCache in the gap. On a cold cache in non-dev mode, N concurrent requests will all pass the initial nil check, then serialize on the write lock and each re-execute the full load (parsing assets-manifest.json, calling cfg.GetContentDeliveryURL, and potentially an HTTP fetch from the CDN once the hardcoded cdn variable is enabled). Only the last result is kept, so the earlier loads are wasted work, and different concurrent callers can receive different *EntryPointAssets instances despite the cache semantics. The standard fix is to re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after acquiring the write lock.

findings.title: No regression test exercising concurrent GetWebAssets calls
findings.body: This PR fixes a data race on the package-level entryPointAssetsCache variable, but adds no test that calls GetWebAssets concurrently (e.g., from multiple goroutines with the race detector enabled via `go test -race`). Without such a test, a future refactor that drops or weakens the mutex guarding would not be caught by CI, and the race this PR fixes would silently regress. A simple test spinning up several goroutines calling GetWebAssets against a temp manifest file in both Dev and non-Dev environments would cover the guarded paths.
